opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES members; researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Not available to cover principal researcher salary, bench fees or departmental vehicle hire; not a scholarship; cannot fund projects forming part of a funded fellowship or undergraduate/master's degree.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation; not required for all group members to be members.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracks innovative and impactful research by funding up to £30,000 over two years for the formation of new synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: up to £500 per year for a decade of data collection (first five years' funding of £3,500 claimable in year 1, additional £3,500 in year 6)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers, consultants and university academics; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies such as restoration, habitat creation, alien species control and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level; no geographical restrictions; awarded to individuals, not organisations; projects max 12 months; funding unavailable for work forming part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Improves the education of future generations of ecologists by providing up to £5,000 towards evidence-based learning, funding research on education methods within ecology to inform teaching and learning practices.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals, not organisations; placements up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20,000 towards placements in different disciplines and sectors, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; projects max 12 months; no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication activities.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: maximum £500 for in-person events, £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdocs, undergraduates and masters students not eligible); work/study at a university or research institution; work in scientific areas within ecology remit; must give a presentation if attending a meeting.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to network and publicise their research by presenting at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering travel, registration, food and accommodation costs up to £1,000. Awarded via a lottery-based system.
